stem: A teenager presents with vomiting, dehydration, acidosis and marked ketonaemia after a period of very low carbohydrate intake, with a serum glucose of 12 mmol/L; which statement best reflects the diagnosis?

options.text: This cannot be diabetic ketoacidosis because the glucose is below 14 mmol/L
This may represent euglycaemic ketoacidosis, which can occur when blood glucose is below 14 mmol/L
Ketoacidosis is excluded unless ketonuria is absent
A glucose below 14 mmol/L means insulin should never be considered relevant
The diagnosis depends mainly on thyroid autoantibodies

explanation: Euglycaemic ketoacidosis is the correct concept. A blood glucose below 14 mmol/L does not exclude ketoacidosis when there is acidosis and marked ketonaemia, especially after starvation or very low carbohydrate intake.

rationale: The key point is that ketoacidosis can occur with glucose below 14 mmol/L, so a normal or only mildly elevated glucose does not rule it out in the right clinical context.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because glucose below 14 mmol/L does not exclude diabetic or euglycaemic ketoacidosis.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because euglycaemic ketoacidosis can occur with blood glucose below 14 mmol/L, particularly in the setting of starvation or low carbohydrate intake.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because ketoacidosis is identified by acidosis with ketonaemia or ketonuria, and the absence of ketonuria is not required to make the diagnosis.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because insulin may still be relevant in ketoacidosis even when the glucose is below 14 mmol/L.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because thyroid autoantibodies are not the basis for diagnosing euglycaemic ketoacidosis.
